Plot saved posterior estimates and credible intervals

Source: R/api-plotting-posterior.R
plot.mfrm_posterior_summary.Rd

Plot saved posterior estimates and credible intervals

Usage 

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_posterior_summary'
plot(
  x,
  quantity = c("location", "ability", "step_offset", "slope", "log_slope",
    "population_mean", "population_sd"),
  facet = NULL,
  draw = TRUE,
  reference = NULL,
  preset = "standard",
  show_legend = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Output from read_mfrm_posterior().

quantity

One of "location" (default), "ability", "step_offset", "slope", "log_slope", "population_mean" or "population_sd". Population quantities require an estimated-population export. Quantities with different units are not mixed.

facet

Optional facet/owner names to retain; NULL retains all for the selected quantity. Step rows use facet = "Step owner" and retain their owner labels and category transitions in the plotted table.

draw

Logical; FALSE returns plot data without opening a device.

reference

Optional finite vertical reference; NULL omits it. Zero for locations and one for relative slopes are references, not standards of performance or rater quality.

preset

A package plot preset, such as "standard" or "monochrome".

show_legend

Logical; show interval/fixed-value symbols.

title, subtitle, caption

Optional returned text. Defaults omit it. Text is not drawn by default; retrieve it with plot_data().

...

Unused.

Value

Invisibly, an mfrm_plot_data with the exact long table, source settings, parameter identities, interval statuses and interpretation notes. as_ggplot() returns an editable ggplot; plot_data() supplies the table for custom graphics. No posterior draws, densities or raincloud samples are reconstructed from marginal summaries.

Details

These are saved equal-tailed 95% posterior credible intervals, not frequentist confidence intervals. Dashed intervals and open circles mark estimates whose sampling screen requires review; solid intervals mean that no sampling flag was detected, not that inference is validated. Open diamonds mark fixed anchors/constraint-determined values without an interval. Crosses mark estimated points without an available interval. Missing points retain their labels and are never replaced by zero. Original row order, labels and endpoints are preserved. The plot never refits, changes the level, selects significant effects or validates priors.

Session plot defaults

Set options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "publication") to choose a session default for plotting functions that expose the common preset argument. The supported values are "standard", "publication", "compact" and "monochrome". Precedence is an explicit call argument, then the session option, then "standard". For example, preset = "standard" overrides a session set to "monochrome". Explicit preset = NULL retains the earlier package-default behavior; it does not read the session option. Invalid session values cause an error only when that option is needed.

The category-curve, data-quality, fit-review, connectivity and network routes of plot() for report bundles use the same option through .... Plots without a common preset argument, including extended-model plots with their own palette controls, keep their own settings. This option selects a preset, not a universal theme or a guarantee that all renderers implement every appearance control identically.

New plot payloads retain the resolved preset for supported saved-data rendering. Converting an existing payload with as_ggplot() uses its saved appearance, even after the session option changes. A call that creates a new plot from a fit or statistical result uses the current default. For a reproducible script, supply preset explicitly or set the option in that script. Saving only the fitted model does not save a session option. No global ggplot theme is changed.

Restore previous settings with old <- options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "monochrome") followed by options(old). Use options(mfrmr.plot_preset = NULL) to remove the option. The preset changes appearance, not estimates, confidence levels or diagnostic thresholds.

See also

read_mfrm_posterior(), mfrm_report()

Examples 

posterior <- read_mfrm_posterior(system.file(
  "extdata", "posterior-example", package = "mfrmr"))
p <- plot(posterior, quantity = "location", draw = FALSE)
plot_data(p, "table")
